rows.value: Map
rows.name: title_2

rows.value: Displays polygons from a data list, and can let the user draw new ones and save them back to that data list.
rows.name: text_3

rows.value: Parameters
rows.name: title_4

rows.value: data_list - name of the data list holding the geometries. Required.
rows.name: text_5

rows.value: geometry_field_name - column holding each geometry. Default: geometry
rows.name: text_6

rows.value: properties_field_name - column holding each feature's properties. Default: properties
rows.name: text_7

rows.value: center_lon, center_lat, zoom - where the map opens when it has no shapes to frame.
rows.name: text_8

rows.value: max_fit_zoom - closest zoom used when framing loaded shapes. Default: 18. Set 0 to always keep center_lon, center_lat and zoom.
rows.name: text_9

rows.value: editable - false displays the shapes without any drawing tools. Default: true
rows.name: text_10

rows.value: filter - limits which data list rows the map uses, written like a data_items filter.
rows.name: text_11

rows.value: save_values - columns stamped on every saved row. Editable maps only.
rows.name: text_12

rows.value: 1. View only
rows.name: title_13

rows.value: editable: false displays the geometries without the drawing tools, so recorded data (e.g. a GPS trace with ids from a server) is shown as it is, rather than having to satisfy the drawing library's rules.
rows.name: text_14

rows.value: 2. Filtering rows
rows.name: title_16

rows.value: filter limits the map to some of the data list, using the same syntax as data_items: @item.column refers to the row, and anything else (@local, @field, @data) is evaluated before the filter runs.
rows.name: text_17

value.fullExpression: filter limits the map to some of the data list, using the same syntax as data_items: @item.column refers to the row, and anything else (@local, @field, @data) is evaluated before the filter runs.

rows.value: A view-only map reloads whenever the filter changes, so changing a local variable it depends on updates the map in place. An editable map does not reload, as that would discard anything drawn but not yet saved.
rows.name: text_18

rows.value: Note: a parameter value is cut at its second colon, so a filter cannot contain a colon. Use == and && as above.
rows.name: text_25

rows.value: 3. Framing the shapes
rows.name: title_26

rows.value: By default the map zooms to fit the shapes it loads, no closer than max_fit_zoom. This matters when the authored centre is nowhere near the data: without it the map opens on empty ground and the shapes have to be hunted for.
rows.name: text_27

rows.value: max_fit_zoom: 0 turns framing off, so the map stays where center_lon, center_lat and zoom put it. The map below opens on the Gulf of Guinea, several thousand km from the shapes it has loaded.
rows.name: text_28

rows.value: 4. Drawing and saving
rows.name: title_30

rows.value: With editable left unset, the drawing tools are shown. The save button writes every drawn feature to data_list, and removes rows the map loaded that are no longer drawn.
rows.name: text_31

rows.value: save_values stamps extra columns onto each saved row, so a feature drawn under a filter still matches that filter when the map is next opened. It uses = rather than : because a parameter value is cut at its second colon.
rows.name: text_32

rows.value: The columns listed in save_values must already exist in the data list sheet. A data list's schema comes from its first row, and any field not in it is silently dropped when saving.
rows.name: text_33

rows.value: Draw a polygon, save, then switch group above and reload the page: the shape is kept with the group that was selected when it was drawn.
rows.name: text_34

rows.value: Notes
rows.name: title_36

rows.value: The id column of the data list must be formatted as plain text in the sheet. Numeric ids fail to load with the error about the ID column needing to be formatted as a string.
rows.name: text_37

rows.value: A map has no height of its own unless it is the only row in its container, so give it a style_list such as height: 400px. Without one the map container is 0 pixels high and nothing is drawn.
rows.name: text_38

rows.value: A geometry cell accepts a GeoJSON Polygon, a GeoJSON Feature, or a plain list of [lon, lat] points. A third value per point (altitude) is ignored, and the ring is closed automatically if the sheet does not close it.
rows.name: text_39

rows.value: Drawing requires geometries the drawing library accepts; recorded data usually does not qualify, which is what editable: false is for.
rows.name: text_40
